# CLI reference

Every `archlang` command, flag, format and exit code — generated from the same capability
manifest that `archlang manifest --json` serves, so this page cannot fall behind the CLI.

The CLI is ArchLang's **primary agent interface**. Every command takes `--json` (structured
result on **stdout**, human messages on **stderr**), and every command that reads source
accepts a file path or `-` for stdin.

```bash
npx -y @chanmeng666/archlang help        # zero-install
npm i -g @chanmeng666/archlang           # or install the archlang command
archlang manifest --json                 # this page, as data
```

`arch` is installed as an alias of `archlang`, but on Linux, macOS and Git Bash coreutils owns
that name, so this page never uses it.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | ok |
| `1` | internal / IO error |
| `2` | user-source error (deterministic — fix it, don't blindly retry) |
| `3` | bad usage |

## Output formats

`-f <format>` on `compile`, `batch`, `md` and `preview`.

| Format | Dependency |
| --- | --- |
| `svg` | zero-dep (built in) |
| `dxf` | zero-dep (built in) |
| `txt` | zero-dep (built in) |
| `json` | zero-dep (built in) |
| `pdf` | needs optional `pdfkit` |
| `png` | needs optional `@resvg/resvg-js` |

## Global flags

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

## Commands

### `archlang compile`

render a plan to SVG/DXF/TXT/PDF/PNG, or to Plan JSON

**Input:** `<file.arch|-> (Plan JSON with --from-json)` · **Output:** file (or stdout with -o -) — with --json and no -o nothing is written

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <file\|->` | output file, or '-' for stdout (default: the input path with the format's extension) |
| `--format, -f <svg\|dxf\|txt\|json\|pdf\|png>` | output format (default svg); json writes the Plan JSON that --from-json reads |
| `--level <n>` | render only this storey of a multi-storey plan (level blocks) to the plain -o target, instead of one &lt;stem&gt;.L&lt;level&gt;.&lt;ext&gt; file per level |
| `--width, -w <px>` | page width hint in pixels |
| `--scale, -s <n>` | raster scale for the PNG backend (ignored by the non-raster formats) |
| `--cols <n>` | text renderer (-f txt / preview --ascii) grid width in characters (default 80) |
| `--charset <unicode\|ascii>` | text renderer glyph set (default unicode) |
| `--overlay <circulation>` | draw an opt-in diagnostic overlay (circulation walks + bottleneck markers); default output is unchanged |
| `--error-svg` | on a broken plan, still emit a self-describing error-card image listing the diagnostics (exit code stays 2); it is an output like any other, so with --json and no -o nothing is written and the card is not in the payload — pass -o &lt;file&gt; to get the image |
| `--accessible` | emit &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt;/role/aria accessibility metadata (the describe() caption) into the SVG; default output is unchanged |
| `--acc-id-prefix <prefix>` | with --accessible, prefix the &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt; element ids (default arch, giving arch-title/arch-desc) so several plans inlined in one HTML page do not share them; ignored without --accessible |
| `--from-json` | read the input as Plan JSON (RPLAN shape) instead of .arch, convert it, then compile |
| `--install` | auto-install the optional dep for the chosen format if missing (PNG/PDF) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |
| `--view <iso\|axon>` | DEPRECATED (removed in 2.0; ArchLang draws plans) — render an illustrative axonometric of the building instead of the plan (iso = true isometric, axon = the 30/60 plan oblique) — a picture, never a measured drawing: no scale, no title block, no dimensions, and `describe`/`lint` are unaffected |

**Examples**

```bash
# render to the named file; structured result on stdout
$ archlang compile plan.arch -o plan.svg --json

# check it compiles and WRITE NOTHING (no -o names a file) — reports written:false, bytes, diagnostics, summary
$ archlang compile plan.arch --json

# render SVG next to the input (plan.svg)
$ archlang compile plan.arch

# compile source from stdin straight to SVG on stdout
$ archlang compile - -o - < plan.arch

# export the Plan JSON; `archlang compile plan.json --from-json` renders it back
$ archlang compile plan.arch -f json -o plan.json

# rasterize to PNG, fetching the optional renderer if it is missing
$ archlang compile plan.arch -f png -o plan.png --install --json

# a multi-storey plan writes one sheet per level (house.L1.svg, house.L2.svg …) and reports outputs[]
$ archlang compile house.arch -o house.svg --json

# render just the upper storey of a multi-storey plan to one file
$ archlang compile house.arch --level 2 -o upper.svg

# an illustrative isometric of the whole building (every storey in ONE drawing, so no per-level fan-out)
$ archlang compile house.arch --view iso -o house-iso.svg
```

### `archlang batch`

render many .arch files in one call, concurrently

**Input:** `<a.arch> <b.arch> …` · **Output:** one file per input; --json gives a results[] array

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <dir>` | output DIRECTORY for every rendered file (default: alongside each input) |
| `--format, -f <svg\|dxf\|txt\|json\|pdf\|png>` | output format (default svg); json writes the Plan JSON that --from-json reads |
| `--jobs, -j <n>` | max concurrent renders (default: CPU count) |
| `--width, -w <px>` | page width hint in pixels |
| `--scale, -s <n>` | raster scale for the PNG backend (ignored by the non-raster formats) |
| `--cols <n>` | text renderer (-f txt / preview --ascii) grid width in characters (default 80) |
| `--charset <unicode\|ascii>` | text renderer glyph set (default unicode) |
| `--overlay <circulation>` | draw an opt-in diagnostic overlay (circulation walks + bottleneck markers); default output is unchanged |
| `--error-svg` | on a broken plan, still emit a self-describing error-card image listing the diagnostics (exit code stays 2) |
| `--accessible` | emit &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt;/role/aria accessibility metadata (the describe() caption) into the SVG; default output is unchanged |
| `--acc-id-prefix <prefix>` | with --accessible, prefix the &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt; element ids (default arch, giving arch-title/arch-desc) so several plans inlined in one HTML page do not share them; ignored without --accessible |
| `--install` | auto-install the optional dep for the chosen format if missing (PNG/PDF) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# render design variants concurrently; one result row per input
$ archlang batch a.arch b.arch c.arch -o out/ --json

# export a whole directory to DXF, 4 renders at a time
$ archlang batch plans/*.arch -f dxf -j 4 --json
```

render every ```arch block in a Markdown file and rewrite to image links

**Input:** `<doc.md>` · **Output:** out.md + one image per block

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <out.md\|->` | rewritten Markdown file, or '-' for stdout (default: &lt;name&gt;.out.md) |
| `--format, -f <svg\|png>` | image format for the blocks (default svg) |
| `--width, -w <px>` | page width hint in pixels |
| `--scale, -s <n>` | raster scale for the PNG backend (ignored by the non-raster formats) |
| `--overlay <circulation>` | draw an opt-in diagnostic overlay (circulation walks + bottleneck markers); default output is unchanged |
| `--error-svg` | on a broken plan, still emit a self-describing error-card image listing the diagnostics (exit code stays 2) |
| `--accessible` | emit &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt;/role/aria accessibility metadata (the describe() caption) into the SVG; default output is unchanged |
| `--acc-id-prefix <prefix>` | with --accessible, prefix the &lt;title&gt;/&lt;desc&gt; element ids (default arch, giving arch-title/arch-desc) so several plans inlined in one HTML page do not share them; ignored without --accessible |
| `--install` | auto-install the optional dep for the chosen format if missing (PNG/PDF) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# render the fenced arch blocks to SVGs and rewrite them to image links
$ archlang md README.md -o README.out.md --json

# PNG images; a broken block still yields an error card
$ archlang md doc.md -f png --error-svg --json
```

### `archlang preview`

render a PNG you can look at (zero-install where the optional binary is present)

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** PNG file (or ASCII text on stdout with --ascii)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <out.png\|->` | output PNG file, or '-' for stdout (default: &lt;name&gt;.png) |
| `--scale, -s <n>` | raster scale (default 1; without -w/-s the page auto-targets ~1600px wide for legibility) |
| `--width, -w <px>` | page width hint in pixels |
| `--ascii` | print a zero-dependency ASCII text plan to stdout instead of a PNG |
| `--level <n>` | preview this storey of a multi-storey plan (default: the lowest level, i.e. page 1) |
| `--cols <n>` | text renderer (-f txt / preview --ascii) grid width in characters (default 80) |
| `--charset <unicode\|ascii>` | text renderer glyph set (default unicode) |
| `--overlay <circulation>` | draw an opt-in diagnostic overlay (circulation walks + bottleneck markers); default output is unchanged |
| `--error-svg` | on a broken plan, still emit a self-describing error-card image listing the diagnostics (exit code stays 2) |
| `--install` | auto-install @resvg/resvg-js if missing, then render |
| `--view <iso\|axon>` | DEPRECATED (removed in 2.0; ArchLang draws plans) — render an illustrative axonometric of the building instead of the plan (iso = true isometric, axon = the 30/60 plan oblique) — a picture, never a measured drawing: no scale, no title block, no dimensions, and `describe`/`lint` are unaffected |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# a zero-dependency text plan an agent can read on stdout
$ archlang preview plan.arch --ascii --json

# raster the plan so a vision model can look at it
$ archlang preview plan.arch -o plan.png --json

# look at one storey of a multi-storey plan
$ archlang preview house.arch --level 2 -o upper.png --json

# raster an illustrative plan-oblique of the building so a vision model can look at it
$ archlang preview house.arch --view axon -o house-axon.png --json
```

### `archlang link`

print a playground URL that opens the plan, rendered, with nothing to install

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** the playground URL; --json gives { ok, playground, embed, bytes } (embed: the plan alone, for an iframe; bytes: the compressed plan). A plan that does not compile still gets a link: ok false with an errors count, one warning on stderr, exit 0

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# a URL to give the user: it opens the plan in the hosted playground
$ archlang link plan.arch

# the playground and embed URLs as data, and whether the plan compiles
$ archlang link plan.arch --json
```

### `archlang validate`

parse + resolve + lint, no render (is it valid & sound?)

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** diagnostics (plus a graph{} report with --graph and an intent{ ok, satisfied, total, subscores, violations } block with --intent), then `next`: the one item to fix first { tier, code, message, span?, hint? } or null (tiers: error, warning, validity, drafting, intent, profile, taste)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--strict, --fail-on-warning` | advisory warnings fail too (exit 2) |
| `--graph <graph.json>` | also check the plan's interior-door adjacency against an intended graph (bare dict or {input_graph:{…}}); mismatch → exit 2 |
| `--intent <intent.json>` | gate the plan against a brief's intent JSON; a failing gating assertion (room count/existence/area/windows) → exit 2. Adjacency/reachability score but never gate. Composes with --graph. |
| `--feedback` | with --intent, append a deterministic per-violation correction prompt (advisory data, never applied) |
| `--profile <residential-basic\|accessibility-advisory\|cn-residential-advisory\|uk-residential-advisory\|us-residential-advisory>` | lint under this advisory ruleset too (as `lint --profile`); its own warnings rank as `next` tier profile |
| `--taste <generic\|cn-residential-advisory\|uk-residential-advisory\|us-residential-advisory>` | let `next` fall back to the lowest-scoring taste criterion (ADR 0032); never gates |
| `--code <CODE[,CODE…]>` | show only diagnostics with these codes — a DISPLAY filter: the exit code and `ok` still come from the unfiltered set |
| `--severity <error\|warning>` | show only diagnostics of this severity — a DISPLAY filter, like --code (never changes the exit code) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# the ship gate: errors and advisory warnings both fail
$ archlang validate plan.arch --strict --json

# gate on a brief's intent contract and get per-violation correction prompts
$ archlang validate plan.arch --intent brief.json --feedback --json

# check interior-door adjacency against an intended room graph
$ archlang validate plan.arch --graph rooms.json --json

# read `next` first: the one diagnostic to fix before anything else, by fixed precedence
$ archlang validate plan.arch --json --taste generic

# read only the blocking errors; `ok` and the exit code still weigh every diagnostic
$ archlang validate plan.arch --severity error --json
```

### `archlang describe`

semantic facts: rooms, areas, adjacency, what doors connect

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** facts (JSON or a summary), narrowed by --room/--zone/--select/--level

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--room <id[,id…]>` | keep only these rooms; doors/windows/openings/furniture narrow to the ones touching them (plan-level facts — bbox, totals, caption — stay whole-plan) |
| `--zone <path[,path…]>` | keep only the rooms declared in these `zone` blocks (nested zones roll up; paths are dotted, e.g. west.galleries) — a DISPLAY filter: `ok` and the exit code still weigh the whole plan |
| `--select <key[,key…]>` | emit only these top-level keys of the --json object (rooms, doors, totals, access, circulation, freedom, …); the ok/plan/units/diagnostics envelope is always kept |
| `--level <n>` | report this storey of a multi-storey plan as the top-level facts (a DISPLAY filter — `ok` and the exit code still weigh the whole plan) |
| `--facts <symmetry\|syntax\|depends[,…]>` | also compute these opt-in facts: `symmetry` (the plan's symmetry group per layer — shell, rooms, full — and its repeated rooms), `syntax` (space-syntax depth, mean depth, RA, integration and control on the access graph) and `depends` (per element, the ids it derives from and the `let`/parameter names it reads); absent by default |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# rooms, areas, adjacency, door connections, caption, freedom — confirm the plan means what you intended
$ archlang describe plan.arch --json

# describe source piped on stdin, no temp file
$ archlang describe - --json < plan.arch

# just the rooms and the totals — keep a big plan's facts inside a bounded context
$ archlang describe plan.arch --select rooms,totals --json

# only those two rooms and the doors/windows/furniture that touch them
$ archlang describe plan.arch --room kitchen,bath --json

# only the west wing's rooms and what touches them; `zones[]` reports every declared wing, its rooms and its area
$ archlang describe museum.arch --zone west --json

# the upper storey's rooms/areas/access as the top-level facts (`levels[]` carries every storey)
$ archlang describe house.arch --level 2 --json

# add the symmetry group per layer, repeated rooms, and space-syntax integration on the access graph
$ archlang describe plan.arch --facts symmetry,syntax --json

# per element, the ids it derives from (`on`) and the `let`/parameter names it reads (`params`) — what follows a change
$ archlang describe plan.arch --facts depends --json --select depends
```

### `archlang score`

continuous intent satisfaction (satisfied/total) as data — the refine-loop reward — or, with --taste, the plan's taste score. Measures, never gates (validate --intent is the gate).

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** --brief: { ok, satisfied, total, score, subscores, violations }; --taste: { profile, ok, score, uncapped, capped, validity, advisory, coverage, subscores, criteria } (exit 0 on a successful measurement, whatever the score)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--brief <intent.json>` | the intent JSON to measure satisfaction against (this or --taste) |
| `--taste <generic\|cn-residential-advisory\|uk-residential-advisory\|us-residential-advisory>` | score taste instead (ADR 0032): sourced criteria in [0,1], capped at 0.5 while a validity lint warning stands; never gates (not with --brief) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# continuous intent satisfaction as the refine-loop reward; always exits 0 on a measurement
$ archlang score plan.arch --brief brief.json --json

# taste advice per criterion with its source and an A_* code; read after lint is clean, never a gate
$ archlang score plan.arch --taste generic --json
```

### `archlang lint`

architectural soundness warnings

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** W_* warnings (narrowed by --code/--severity; `filtered`/`total_diagnostics` mark a filtered result), then a `coverage` block naming the rule families skipped and why

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--profile <residential-basic\|accessibility-advisory\|cn-residential-advisory\|uk-residential-advisory\|us-residential-advisory>` | advisory ruleset |
| `--strict, --fail-on-warning` | warnings fail (exit 2) |
| `--code <CODE[,CODE…]>` | show only diagnostics with these codes — a DISPLAY filter: the exit code and `ok` still come from the unfiltered set |
| `--severity <error\|warning>` | show only diagnostics of this severity — a DISPLAY filter, like --code (never changes the exit code) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# architectural soundness warnings as data, each with a fix
$ archlang lint plan.arch --json

# gate on the accessibility ruleset (any warning exits 2)
$ archlang lint plan.arch --profile accessibility-advisory --strict

# read only the reachability warnings; the exit code still reflects every diagnostic
$ archlang lint plan.arch --code W_ROOM_UNREACHABLE,W_NO_ENTRANCE --json
```

### `archlang complete`

completion items in scope at a source byte offset (the LSP completion() core)

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** { items: [...] } completion items

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--at <byteOffset>` | source byte offset to list completions at (required) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# what may legally be written at byte offset 120
$ archlang complete plan.arch --at 120 --json

# completions for source on stdin
$ archlang complete - --at 0 --json < plan.arch
```

### `archlang repair`

explicit source-to-source corrector (furniture out of walls) + change log

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** corrected source + change log on stderr

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <file\|->` | output file for the corrected source, or '-' for stdout (default: stdout) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# the geometric corrector: `source` + a `changes[]` log of every furniture move
$ archlang repair plan.arch --json

# write the corrected source to a new file
$ archlang repair plan.arch -o repaired.arch
```

### `archlang fix`

apply the machine-applicable fix suggestions on a plan's diagnostics (bounded fixpoint)

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** fixed source (to the input file or -o) + a unified diff and change log on stderr

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <file\|->` | output file for the fixed source, or '-' for stdout (default: rewrite the input file in place) |
| `--unsafe` | also apply `maybe-incorrect` fixes (default: machine-applicable only) |
| `--dry-run` | compute the result but do not write it (the diff preview still prints) |
| `--backup` | before rewriting a file in place, save the original bytes to &lt;file&gt;.bak |
| `--force` | keep a pass even if it raises the error count |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# preview the exact unified diff `fix` would write, changing nothing on disk
$ archlang fix plan.arch --dry-run

# the same preview as data: which fixes would be applied, plus the `diff` they produce
$ archlang fix plan.arch --dry-run --json

# apply the machine-applicable fixes in place, keeping the original as plan.arch.bak
$ archlang fix plan.arch --backup --json

# also apply the maybe-incorrect fixes, leaving the input untouched
$ archlang fix plan.arch -o fixed.arch --unsafe --json
```

### `archlang finish`

furnish the rooms that hold no furniture, then add the sheet statements a plan lacks (paper, scale, dims auto, title, schedule rooms, legend); deletes nothing

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** finished source (to the input file or -o) + a unified diff and change log on stderr

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <file\|->` | output file for the finished source, or '-' for stdout (default: rewrite the input file in place) |
| `--only <sheet\|furnish>` | run only this stage (available: sheet, furnish; default: furnish, then sheet) |
| `--reissue` | allow `paper` and `scale` (nothing else) to be replaced when the drawing does not fit the authored sheet |
| `--dry-run` | compute the result but do not write it (the diff preview still prints) |
| `--backup` | before rewriting a file in place, save the original bytes to &lt;file&gt;.bak |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# preview the furniture and sheet statements `finish` would add: `changes[]`, `unresolved[]` and the `diff`
$ archlang finish plan.arch --dry-run --json

# complete the drawing in place once lint is clean, keeping the original as plan.arch.bak
$ archlang finish plan.arch --backup

# preview only the furniture: one `furniture` statement per piece, and each room left empty with the reason
$ archlang finish plan.arch --only furnish --dry-run --json

# also replace a paper/scale the drawing does not fit, leaving the input untouched
$ archlang finish plan.arch --reissue -o issued.arch
```

### `archlang reroll`

offer a proven-equivalent `for` loop for a repeated statement run

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** suggestions (JSON or a summary), or the rewritten file with --write

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--write` | apply every non-overlapping suggestion and re-verify the combined result's compiled SVG is byte-identical to the original before writing (no --dry-run/--backup: a failed re-verify writes nothing, and every suggestion is already proven byte-for-byte before it is offered) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# each candidate run as { span, replacement, count, loopVar, tokensBefore, tokensAfter }
$ archlang reroll plan.arch --json

# splice in every proven loop; { ok, wrote, target, applied, skipped } (wrote/target as in `archlang fix`)
$ archlang reroll plan.arch --write --json
```

### `archlang impact`

change one number: what moved and why, what held, what broke

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** { ok, set?, lets, changed[] (each with its `why` dependency chain and `root`), held[], diagnostics: { broke, healed, unchanged_count }, summary } (exit 0 on a report, 2 on a refused --set)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--set <NAME=value>` | override the root plan's top-level `let NAME` with a numeric literal (`4500` is mm, `4.5m`) and compare the plan before and after; refused with E_SET_OVERRIDE when NAME is not exactly one top-level let |
| `--against <old.arch>` | compare the input (the new version) against this older file instead; exactly one of --set and --against |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# widen by one number: every moved/resized/re-hosted element with the chain that moved it, what held, what broke
$ archlang impact plan.arch --set W=4500 --json

# the same report between two versions of a plan (old.arch before, plan.arch after)
$ archlang impact plan.arch --against old.arch
```

### `archlang suggest`

advisory topology suggestions as data (door/window statements that resolve reachability/window faults)

**Input:** `<file.arch|->` · **Output:** suggestions (JSON or a summary)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# ready-to-paste door/window statements for unreachable rooms, no entrance, or a windowless bedroom
$ archlang suggest plan.arch --json
```

### `archlang manifest` _(alias: `capabilities`)_

this document: the whole CLI API as structured data

**Input:** `none` · **Output:** the manifest (JSON or a summary)

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# discover every command, flag, format, and error code in one call
$ archlang manifest --json
```

### `archlang spec`

print the one-prompt language spec (spec.llm.md)

**Input:** `none` · **Output:** the spec

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# the whole language on one page — read this before authoring
$ archlang spec
```

### `archlang context`

print the full bundled agent context (spec + workflow + CLI + errors)

**Input:** `none` · **Output:** the full agent context (llms-full.txt), or one --section of it

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--section <spec\|workflow\|cli\|errors>` | print only one section of the bundle instead of all 136 KB of it (spec = the language, 30 KB; workflow = the agent loop, 28 KB; cli = every command, 24 KB; errors = the diagnostic catalog, 52 KB) |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# the cold-start bundle: spec + workflow + CLI reference + every diagnostic
$ archlang context

# just the diagnostic catalog (52 KB) — read one section instead of paying for the whole 136 KB bundle
$ archlang context --section errors
```

### `archlang new` _(alias: `init`)_

scaffold a starter .arch

**Input:** `none` · **Output:** starter source

| Flag | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `--out, -o <file\|->` | output file — refuses to overwrite an existing one without --force (default: stdout) |
| `--force` | overwrite an existing file |
| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |
| `--quiet, -q` | suppress human messages on stderr |

**Examples**

```bash
# get the starter plan as a `template` string, writing nothing
$ archlang new --json

# scaffold a starter file to edit
$ archlang new -o plan.arch
```

| `--json` | structured result on stdout, messages on stderr |

$ archlang explain E_ROOM_SIZE --json
